title: Access code serves as unique identifier
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest could serve as a unique reference to identify the data subject's access event, potentially linking the guest to the home access system.
assumptions: The access code is logged and stored by the system, creating a record that can be traced back to the guest.

title: Sensitive access code data collected
description: The access code is sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required. The system collects this data to unlock the door, but the sensitivity level may exceed functional necessity.
assumptions: Access codes are considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations.

title: Potential unnecessary data analysis
description: The system may analyze or process the access code beyond what is functionally needed to simply unlock the door, such as logging, storing, or analyzing access patterns.
assumptions: The system logs access events for security or audit purposes, which may constitute unnecessary processing.
uncertainty_note: Depends on system design - some logging may be necessary for security.

title: Guest unaware of data collection
description: The guest may not be fully aware that their access code entry is being recorded, stored, or processed by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate what data is collected during access code entry.

title: Limited control over access data processing
description: The guest may have limited ability to set preferences or control how their access data is processed, stored, or shared by the system.
assumptions: The system may not provide options for the guest to control data retention or processing preferences.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than actually needed to achieve the functional goal of unlocking the door, such as storing access codes longer than necessary.
assumptions: GDPR and similar regulations require data minimization - only collecting and processing what is strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Depends on system design and data retention policies.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in sensor events
description: Motion/door/sensor events may contain unique identifiers (device IDs, timestamps, location data) that can link data to specific individuals or events
assumptions: Events contain identifiable metadata that can be correlated

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of event types, timestamps, and locations can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals
assumptions: Multiple event attributes can be combined to identify individuals

title: Quasi-identifiers in sensor event data
description: Timestamps, event types, and location data form quasi-identifiers that can identify individuals from their behavior patterns
assumptions: Event metadata contains sufficient identifying attributes

title: Revealing attributes in event data
description: The nature of events (door opened, motion detected) reveals information about individuals' presence and activities
assumptions: Event types reveal personal information about individuals

title: Event logs provide non-repudiation evidence
description: Event logs can be used to prevent individuals from denying certain claims about their actions (e.g., door access, motion events)
assumptions: Logs are tamper-resistant and can be attributed to specific events

title: Potentially sensitive sensor data types collected
description: Motion and door events may be perceived as sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required
assumptions: Sensor data reveals personal presence and activities

title: Event retention may exceed functional necessity
description: Sensor events may be stored longer than functionally needed for the home hub's operation
assumptions: No clear retention policy defined for event logs

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subjects
description: Individuals may not be aware that their motion/door/sensor events are being logged and stored
assumptions: No clear notification or consent mechanism for event logging

title: Lack of control over data collection preferences
description: Data subjects may have limited ability to set preferences or consent regarding which sensor events are collected
assumptions: No user controls for event logging configuration

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (sensor events) may be processed than is actually needed for the home hub's functional goals
assumptions: Event logging may exceed functional requirements

title: Linking through device/user identifiers in motion alerts
description: The real-time motion alert forwarded from Home Hub may contain device identifiers, user IDs, or other unique references that could link the motion event to a specific individual or device.
assumptions: Motion alerts may include metadata containing identifiers
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion alerts contain some form of identifier

title: Quasi-identifier combining in motion data
description: Motion data combined with other available data (e.g., location, time, device type) could serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Motion data can be combined with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Depends on what other data is available in the system

title: Processing of identified data in motion alerts
description: The motion alert may contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (e.g., user ID, device ID) that are processed during transmission.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain identifiable user references
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion alerts are associated with specific users

title: Detection through observed communications
description: The transmission of motion alerts from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend could be observed by third parties, revealing that motion events are occurring.
assumptions: Communication channel is observable
uncertainty_note: Depends on encryption and network security

title: Excessive data type sensitivity
description: Motion data may be more sensitive than functionally required for the alert functionality, potentially revealing more personal information than necessary.
assumptions: Motion data contains personal information beyond what's needed for alerts
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific motion data being transmitted

title: Data propagation to other services
description: Motion data forwarded to Mobile App Backend may be further propagated to other services where it is not functionally needed.
assumptions: Mobile App Backend shares data with other services
uncertainty_note: Assuming backend may share data with third parties

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and forwarded to the Mobile App Backend.
assumptions: Users are not informed about motion data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on privacy policy and user consent mechanisms

title: Lack of user control over motion data preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed and shared.
assumptions: No granular consent controls for motion data
uncertainty_note: Depends on UI/UX design and consent mechanisms

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing motion data may exceed what is actually needed for the alert functionality, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Motion data collection exceeds functional requirements

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Motion data received at Mobile App Backend may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including predetermined third parties.
assumptions: Backend shares data with known third parties
uncertainty_note: Assuming backend has data sharing arrangements

title: Lack of data subject access control
description: Users may lack control in accessing the motion data that is being processed at the Mobile App Backend.
assumptions: Users cannot access their motion data

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The video clip stored in the cloud is identified data associated with a specific homeowner, and is being retrieved and processed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: The video is linked to a specific homeowner identity in the system.

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content may reveal personal attributes about the homeowner (e.g., location, activities, possessions) that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Video content contains observable personal information about the homeowner.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be perceived as more sensitive than strictly required for the playback functionality.
assumptions: Video data contains sensitive personal information about the homeowner.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: The video may be processed, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is functionally needed for simple playback (e.g., metadata extraction, content analysis).
assumptions: The system may perform additional processing on the video beyond playback.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if additional processing occurs beyond playback.

title: Homeowner unawareness of video processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of how their video data is being processed, stored, or accessed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not fully disclose all processing activities.

title: Lack of homeowner control over video processing
description: The homeowner may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular consent controls for video data.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the playback functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this system and video data processing exceeds functional necessity.
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual system design and data minimization practices.

title: Video data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: The video data retrieved by the mobile app backend may be accessible to more parties (e.g., other services, third parties) than functionally necessary for playback.
assumptions: The mobile app backend may share or propagate video data to other systems.
uncertainty_note: Depends on backend architecture and data sharing policies.
